text:
emma_customer: Hi team — AcmePay just flagged a big increase in confidently-wrong answers after last night's rollout. They say responses now assert specific partner names, regulatory links, and fee numbers that are false. :warning:

linda_cs: Thanks, emma. Can you paste one or two concrete examples from the customer? Even short prompt+response pairs help.

emma_customer: Sure — they sent two. First one (user asked for "list the third-party processors AcmePay uses for ACH"):
```
User prompt: "Which third-party processors does AcmePay use for ACH settlement?"
Model reply: "AcmePay uses FastWire, ClearTransit, and Northbank for ACH. For regulatory guidance see https://acmepay.com/compliance/ach-guidelines-2025.pdf"
```
Notes: all three vendor names are wrong and the link 404s. Previously model returned a safer "I don't have access to that customer-specific info" or suggested how to check account settings.

emma_customer: Second repro (billing question):
```
User prompt: "What are the interchange fees AcmePay charges for business accounts?"
Model reply: "AcmePay charges a flat 1.8% + $0.10 per transaction for business debit, and 2.9% + $0.30 for credit. See https://acmepay.com/pricing/business-2024.pdf"
```
Customer says these numbers are made up and contradict their published pricing.

linda_cs: Oof. Did they note whether this happens only on long contexts or certain routes?

emma_customer: Happens across a few routes. They tried our hosted API and a Dedicated instance (ded-nyc-1). More common on conversations that have >800 tokens but also seen on short prompts.

mike_eng: @linda_cs thanks. Can you capture the API request metadata (model, model_version, temperature, top_p, system prompt, routing policy)? Also need the exact request_id if available.

emma_customer: They attached one request log:
```json
{ "model": "redwood-4b-std", "model_version": "v2.8-canary", "temperature": 0.0, "top_p": 1.0, "route": "fastpath-low-latency", "request_id": "rq_8a7f3c" }
```

emma_customer: They also tested pinning model_version to "v2.7.4" and said the hallucinations dropped sharply.

jana_ml: Interesting — mark me in. We had a runtime change in v2.8 that tweaks prefix-KV caching and a kernel selection tweak for attention for long contexts. Could be a cache-priming bug.

owen_infra: Canary deploy logs: deploy-bot reports:
"deploy-bot: canary deploy completed 2026-03-16T02:10:00Z - service inference-api v2.8-canary -> cluster-3 (10% traffic)"

mike_eng: If pinning to v2.7.4 fixes it that narrows things. Jana, do we have any unit tests covering hallucination/regression for model outputs?

jana_ml: We run quality checks but mostly sampling-level metrics; not specific to invented proper nouns. I'll spin up a small eval suite against AcmePay-like prompts.

linda_cs: Customer asked for a mitigation: they want immediate options to avoid bad outputs in production. Suggestions?

mike_eng: Quick mitigations: 1) Pin them to v2.7.4 (we can override routing) 2) Force-suppress entity hallucinations by adding a system instruction like "If you don't know, say 'I don't have that information'" 3) Lower temperature to 0 and add verification step in prompt.

emma_customer: They've already pinned to v2.7.4 temporarily. Would like a root cause and ETA.

jana_ml: I'll reproduce locally with the same model binary + v2.8 serving config (KV caching enabled + attention optimization flag). If I can repro, we push a hotfix to revert the cache priming change.

owen_infra: FYI the canary rollout included a small tokenization tweak in the request preprocessor in cluster-3. Noted in infra changelog. Could affect prompt parsing.

mike_eng: Good catch. Tokenization + KV priming + attention kernel change — multiple potential factors. Prioritize: 1) reproduce using exact request payload 2) try with/without tokenization tweak 3) try with/without KV priming.

jana_ml: Repro plan: run redwood-4b-std:v2.8-canary locally against the two prompts at context lengths 32, 512, 1024. Capture logits and attention patterns.

emma_customer: Customer also provided a sample curl they used to hit hosted API: 
```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-4b-std","model_version":"v2.8-canary","input":"Which third-party processors..."}'
```

linda_cs: Thanks. I'll open a ticket with severity P1 and attach logs and the customer's screenshots.

mike_eng: If we confirm a regression, we should rollback the canary and block the full rollout until a fix is out.

jana_ml: On it. I'll aim for a first reproducible result in 6-8 hours and report back in this thread.

emma_customer: Customer is asking for an ETA for rollback or a config bypass. They prefer rollback to 2.7.4 if possible.

owen_infra: Ops: we can throttle canary traffic or route AcmePay's org to v2.7.4 via routing override. I can do that now if requested.

linda_cs: Please do the routing override for AcmePay org_id=org_1204 while we investigate.

owen_infra: Done — override applied. Confirmed traffic for org_1204 -> redwood-4b-std:v2.7.4.

emma_customer: Customer confirms immediate drop in bad answers after override. Thanks.

jana_ml: Repro attempt queued. Will update with logs and proposed fix path.

mike_eng: Thanks all. Please add any new artifacts to ticket CS-4932. :thumbsup:
